title: Returned-Payment History and the Rental Late-Renewal Pay-In-Full Rate
content:
**Rate rule.** The pay-in-full discount rate of a Rental Property Service Contracts late-renewal premium follows the returned payments billed back on the contract in the thirty-six months before the late renewal:

| Returned payments billed back on the contract in the 36 months before the late renewal | Pay-in-full discount rate |
|---|---|
| two or more | 0.05 |
| exactly one | 0.08 |
| none | the tier's own pay-in-full discount rate (0.10 on every tier) |

**Records read.** The returned payment charges in the contract's billing history and their dates.

**How the rate acts.** It is the pay-in-full discount rate by which twelve base monthly amounts are reduced in pricing the late-renewal premium, the reduction multiplying with the portfolio reduction.

## Hypothetical contracts

- Two returned payments, 30 and 14 months before the late renewal: 0.05.
- One returned payment 20 months before, another 40 months before: only one falls in the 36 months, so 0.08.
- No returned payment in the 36 months: 0.10.

*Worked figure:* Bridgewell Rental Combo, one unit, portfolio rate 0.05, one returned payment in the window: twelve times $64.99 is $779.88; reduced by 0.08 it is $717.4896; reduced by 0.05 it is $681.61512.
